definition: Two variants of a router that decides per query whether a hybrid model should think or answer directly: a 'trained' router learned from data, and an 'oracle' router with perfect foresight of which mode would have been correct, used as an upper-bound comparison. OptimalThinkingBench finds a trained router improves its combined F1^otb metric 20.4% on average over the best single mode, but still trails the oracle router by roughly 15 points -- showing real routers leave most of the achievable gain on the table.

evidence.note: Introduces OptimalThinkingBench, a unified benchmark pairing OverthinkingBench (simple queries) and UnderthinkingBench (hard reasoning/math) with a shared F1 metric, showing that none of 33 evaluated LLMs balances accuracy and thinking-token efficiency.
evidence.title: OptimalThinkingBench: Evaluating Over and Underthinking in LLMs

name: trained difficulty-based router / oracle router
